class_id: measuring a symptom of a fix that is merged but not deployed
feature: any investigation that measures live/staging data to characterise a defect; scripts/ops/merged-not-deployed.mjs and the SessionStart brief that prints its count
symptom: a defect is measured on live data, its population and growth rate are established, and a fix is scoped — while the fix already exists on origin/main, unreachable from the latest prod-* tag. Every number measured is real and every conclusion drawn from it is wrong in the same way: the growth rate is the rate at which UNDEPLOYED code fails, not the rate at which a defect grows. The tell is a measurement whose window sits entirely after a fix commit's merge date. Universal shape: measuring production behaviour characterises the DEPLOYED code, never the code on main, and the two are only the same when a deploy has happened since the last merge. A count of merged-not-deployed commits printed as a bare number is read as background noise; resolved to identities it names exactly which defects the measurement cannot be about.
first_seen: 2026-09-20 — issue #762. Parked ipo_field_plan rows measured at 12,480 (2026-09-18) and 13,980 (2026-09-20), giving ~750/day, and reported as an accumulating leak needing a re-queue mechanism. The re-queue mechanism had been merged the day before: PR #763, commit 2bdcea47, 2026-09-19 01:31 IST, after three review rounds. Verified: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2bdcea47 origin/main` true, `... 2bdcea47 prod-2026-09-07` FALSE, newest prod tag twelve days older than the fix, both walk flags opt-in and default off. The growth measured was production running pre-fix code. The SessionStart hook had printed `fixed on main, still not on prod: 190` at the top of the same session and it was read as background noise
fix_prs: no code fix — the remedy is a deploy, and the detection already exists. scripts/ops/merged-not-deployed.mjs (T-498) lists every fix/feat commit on origin/main not reachable from the latest prod-* tag, with issue numbers and days-since-merge, and it ran at session start. The gap is consumption, not detection: a bare count of 190 was printed and not resolved to identities, which signal-ownership.md R1 forbids for exactly this reason
detection_check: scripts/ops/merged-not-deployed.mjs already covers the class and already runs. What is missing is the consuming step: before measuring any live population to characterise a defect, run it with --json and check whether the issue's own number appears in the merged-not-deployed list. If it does, the measurement characterises undeployed code and must say so. A natural upgrade is for the SessionStart brief to name the issue numbers for the oldest merged-not-deployed commits rather than printing a bare count, so the 190 arrives as identities
